So, some users here think that downvotes should only be used for spam, and not to show disagreement with their content. This is a problem because past 3 or 4 downvotes the comment collapses and many will just skip it because they think it was spam while, most of the times, it is just expressing an unpopular opinion.

A possibile solution to this problem is to only leave upvotes that will bring comments at the top of the thread and then only have a SPAM/OT button to vote if that comment is or not spam/off-topic. When enough people marks the comment as spam the comment is collapsed (exactly as it happens now with downvotes) but when you mark a comment as spam you should also leave a brief message with the reason. If you report too many comments as spam/ot when they aren't you might lose the ability to "report spam/ot" for some time (or completely).

In this way we would still have a mean to bring interesting comments at the top of the thread, we would solve the problem of hiding comments only because they have unpopular opinions, we would solve the "brigading" problem, and we would also know that collapsed comments are actually spam and we would discourage revenges and make it clear that collapsed comments are only for spam.

It would also be cool to mark the comment as "interesting", "funny", etc in a democratic way as suggested here https://voat.co/v/ideasforvoat/comments/815981 .
The people who downvoat opinions they disagree with will probably use the SPAM/OT button to collapse non-spam opinions they disagree with.

That is why the users should leave a brief comment with the reason why they think it is SPAM/OT. These comments would be visible to the moderators and, perhaps, to the author of the comment too that could, somehow, appeal to the moderator.

If a user is caught using the SPAM/OT button for reasons different than its purpose this ability could be suspended or removed (for that specific ab-user).

I think that this would greatly discourage the so said "soft-censorship" that we see happening here regularly.

Seems tough to implement, but i like this idea.
